title: Christ Our Righteousness
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ our righteousness means that the believer’s standing before God rests on the righteousness of Jesus Christ, not on personal merit, religious effort, or moral performance. In Him, sinners are counted righteous by grace through faith.
summary: Christ our righteousness means that the believer’s standing before God rests on the righteousness of Jesus Christ, not on personal merit, religious effort, or moral performance. In Him, sinners are counted righteous by grace through faith.
christFocus: Jesus fulfilled righteousness and became righteousness for His people. His obedience and saving work provide the only secure standing sinners can have before the holy God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sinners need more than forgiveness of wrongdoing. They need righteousness before God. Fallen people cannot produce the righteousness God requires, but Christ provides it.

Jesus obeyed perfectly and gave Himself for sinners. Scripture teaches that God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.

This righteousness is received by faith, not achieved by works. Paul counted his own religious righteousness as loss in order to gain Christ and be found in Him.

Christ our righteousness gives believers a firm standing before God. Their acceptance is not rooted in mood, progress, ministry success, or comparison, but in the finished work and righteousness of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers live under constant fear that they are not enough. In themselves, they are not. But the Gospel does not ask them to stand before God in themselves; it gives them Christ.

This doctrine destroys both pride and despair. No one can boast in their own righteousness, and no believer must despair as though Christ’s righteousness were insufficient.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop trying to establish your own righteousness before God. Trust Christ as your righteousness, confess sin honestly, and obey from gratitude rather than fear. Help others look away from self-measurement and toward the Savior who is enough.
